hook: A grainy monochrome still image captured by a U.S. military system in 2025, showing two dark irregular objects in the upper right quadrant, submitted by the FBI to AARO as a UAP report with no accompanying mission report.
why_it_matters: This image represents one of the rare instances where a U.S. military sensor captured what the operating crew could not identify, and the FBI chose to formally submit it to AARO under the new UAP reporting framework. The absence of a mission report and the presence of pre-submission redactions limit what analysts can assess, illustrating a recurring transparency gap in the disclosure pipeline. The admitted date/time error in the image metadata further complicates any effort to correlate this sighting with other events or sensor records.

key_findings.finding: Two dark, irregular-shaped objects were captured by the military sensor just right of center in the upper right quadrant of the frame.
The operator who collected the imagery was unable to positively identify the UAP, satisfying the threshold for formal AARO submission.
The original imagery was altered with redactions before being submitted to AARO, and no accompanying mission report was provided, reducing the evidentiary value of the submission.
The date embedded in the image is acknowledged to be incorrect due to the system's date/time not having been properly set, making temporal correlation with other events unreliable.
The image was sourced from a U.S. military system and reported through the FBI, indicating a military-to-law-enforcement reporting chain rather than a direct military-to-AARO submission.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The FBI formally submitted this military sensor image to AARO as part of the post-NDAA UAP reporting framework, making AARO the direct institutional recipient and custodian of this evidence.

The image originates from an unspecified U.S. military sensor system, connecting loosely to the broader infrastructure of military UAP collection that historically centered on Wright-Patterson Air Force Base analysis functions.
